title: ANDS Studio — Guided filing journey
walkthrough:
You land on a page with a top bar reading "ANDS Studio" and the tagline "file a drug like a story", plus chips for "My dossiers" and "Portfolio". The hero headline says "File a drug with Health Canada, like telling a story." with a paragraph promising step-by-step guidance and "No regulatory background needed." You click the button "Start my submission →" (a link below offers "Or open your dossiers — every product in submission →"); small print notes "Grounded in real Health Canada process · your progress is saved automatically".

The screen splits into three columns. A left rail titled "Your filing journey" lists the steps: completed ones show a checkmark and "Done", the current one says "You're here", and later ones show a padlock with a plain-language reason for being locked; locked steps cannot be clicked. The centre panel is a step card labelled "Step 1 of 10". The right column shows a 3D "Submission tower" that fills as you progress, and a "Readiness" card reading "● BLOCKED" (later "● READY TO FILE"), a progress bar, tile grid, and — when blocked — the line "The single thing standing between you and ready:" with a button to jump there.

Step 1 asks "Tell me about your drug": fields "What's your drug?", a dropdown "What are you filing?" (e.g. "Generic of an approved brand (ANDS)"), "Dosage form", and a checkbox "It's for a new use the brand isn't approved for". You click "Check my pathway" and get a routing verdict plus warning advisories.

Next you enter "Your Health Canada Company ID" — a 5-digit number you must already hold (placeholder "e.g. 12345"); the teaching text says to request it from the Office of Submission and Intellectual Property if you lack one. Then the "Dossier ID" step requires the one-letter-plus-6–7-digit format (placeholder "e123456"); on leaving the field you see "✓ Valid Dossier ID format." or an error. The submission step asks "Applicant (your company name)" and "Drug product" (pre-filled from earlier answers).

The content step links out: "Open the Module builder →" opens a separate dossier workspace; the main button stays disabled with the hint "Place the required documents to continue" until a counter of missing documents reaches zero and shows "✓ All required documents are in — you can continue."

Remaining steps run validation ("✓ Validation passed…" or an error count), a fees checkbox "My small-business status is already granted" (unchecking warns about forfeiting the discount), internal review, e-signature, then transmission — three receipt tiles "FDA MDN", "FDA ACK", "HC ACK (Core ID)" — and finally tracking of Health Canada's review.
